readings: Taking 20.99 as the cutoff, count a film as expensive to replace only if its `replacement_cost` is strictly greater than 20.99 (so films costing exactly 20.99 are excluded). Look only at those expensive films and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average `length` (ignoring missing values), and the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Leave all values unrounded.

Taking 20.99 as the cutoff, count a film as expensive to replace if its `replacement_cost` is greater than or equal to 20.99 (so films costing exactly 20.99 are included). Look only at those expensive films and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average `length` (ignoring missing values), and the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Leave all values unrounded.
queries:
SELECT rating, AVG(length), AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration)
FROM film
WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99
GROUP BY rating;
SELECT rating, AVG(length), AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration)
FROM film
WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99
GROUP BY rating;
